name: Michio Matsui
current_role: Advisor (former President & Representative Director, 1995-2020), Matsui Securities Co., Ltd.
profile: Michio Matsui (b. 1953, born Mutai) married into the Matsui family and ran Matsui Securities as president for 25 years (1995-2020). He turned a tiny Tokyo broker into a pioneer of Japanese online brokerage, entering internet trading in earnest in 1998. He handed the presidency to Akira Warita in June 2020 and now serves as an advisor.
interesting_fact: Before finance he spent 11 years at shipping line NYK (Nippon Yusen) after graduating from Hitotsubashi in 1976; he joined Matsui Securities in 1987 as a mid-career hire and became president just eight years later.
deep_cut_fact: As a Tokyo high-school student he hung out in jazz cafes, was friends with singer Tatsuro Yamashita, and was in the art club aiming for Tokyo University of the Arts until a teacher talked him out of it.

public_contacts.value: https://www.matsui.co.jp/company/history/essay/ (Matsui Securities page hosting his memoir as former president)

notes: Wealth shared with wife Chizuko Matsui (daughter of the previous president). Retired from management; best route is likely via Matsui Securities corporate office. Speaks/writes in Japanese.

name: Richard Warke
current_role: Founder, Augusta Group of Companies; Executive Chairman, Titan Mining Corp.; Chairman, Solaris Resources
profile: Vancouver-based mining financier who founded the Augusta Group in 2005 and built and sold a string of discoveries: Ventana Gold (Colombia, 2011), Augusta Resource (Rosemont copper, 2014) and Arizona Mining (Hermosa-Taylor zinc, sold to South32 for C$2.1B in 2018); Augusta Gold went to AngloGold Ashanti in 2025. Today he chairs Titan Mining (zinc and New York natural flake graphite), Highlander Silver and Solaris Resources.
interesting_fact: Beyond mining he holds sports stakes: he is a partner in Fenway Sports Group (Boston Red Sox, Liverpool FC) and, per Wikipedia, in the PGA Tour and the Boston Celtics.
deep_cut_fact: Energy-transition angle: his Titan Mining is positioning itself as an emerging US natural flake graphite supplier (a battery material) from its zinc mine in upstate New York; he also co-founded Equinox Gold in 2017.
notes: Low media profile; best route is via Titan Mining / Augusta Group IR in Vancouver. Graphite (battery supply chain) is a natural hook for an energy podcast.

name: Chen Wenping
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager, Sailvan Times Co., Ltd. (赛维时代, SZSE ChiNext: 301381)
profile: Chen Wenping (陈文平) founded Shenzhen-based Sailvan Times in 2012 as a cross-border e-commerce seller and built it into a brand incubator selling fashion and lifestyle products to overseas consumers via Amazon and other platforms. Sailvan listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in July 2023; Chen is the controlling shareholder with roughly 37% and remains chairman.
interesting_fact: Sailvan describes itself as a technology-driven 'smart commerce platform' organised as a 'small front-end + big middle platform' structure, combining product design, brand incubation and supply-chain integration for global online shoppers.
notes: Very low public profile; little personal biography online in English. Country blank in input but he and the company are mainland China (Shenzhen). Route via Sailvan investor relations / board secretary.

name: Hiroyuki Inoue
profile: Hiroyuki Inoue (井上浩行, b. 1945) is the son of Yamato Kogyo founder Asaji Inoue and spent his entire career at the Himeji electric-arc-furnace steelmaker, joining in 1969 and serving as president for about 36 years (1981-2017). He internationalised the company into the US, Thailand, Korea and the Middle East, and has been chairman since 2017 while remaining its largest shareholder (~12%).
interesting_fact: Yamato Kogyo makes rails and switches for Japan's Shinkansen bullet trains, and earns the majority of its sales overseas.
deep_cut_fact: In 1987, under his presidency, Yamato Kogyo formed a joint venture with US steelmaker Nucor, Nucor-Yamato Steel in Arkansas, taking the company into North American H-beam (structural steel) production; it later added JVs in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia.
notes: Re-elected director at June 2025 AGM (94.4% approval). Electric-arc-furnace (low-carbon) steel is a possible energy angle. Japanese-language approach via corporate office recommended.

name: Peter-Alexander Wacker
current_role: Chair of the Supervisory Board, Wacker Chemie AG (since 2008; re-elected 2023)
profile: Great-grandson of founder Alexander Wacker, he owns roughly 10% of Munich-based Wacker Chemie. After ten years at BMW he joined Wacker's board in 1993, became CEO when it went public in 2005, and moved to chair the supervisory board in 2008. Wacker is a major maker of silicones and of hyperpure polysilicon for solar cells and semiconductors.
interesting_fact: Energy/chips angle: Wacker began producing polysilicon, the base material for solar cells and semiconductors, at a new plant in Bradley County (Charleston), Tennessee, in 2016.
deep_cut_fact: He collects elephant figures from around the world because elephants symbolize strength to him, which is why his holding company is named Blue Elephant. He was also named Germany's family businessman of the year in 2006.

public_contacts.value: Manuela.Dollinger@wacker.com (Wacker Media Relations, as listed in company profile)

notes: Holds a doctorate (listed as Dr.). Polysilicon for solar and semiconductors is a strong energy/data-center hook. Approach via Wacker corporate communications in Munich.

name: Family March
current_role: Family group; led today by Juan March de la Lastra, chairman of Banca March (since 2015) and of Corporación Financiera Alba (since Sept 2025)
profile: The March family of Mallorca, descendants of financier Juan March Ordinas (founder of Banca March in 1926), control Banca March and the investment holding Corporación Financiera Alba, which was taken private by family members after a delisting tender offer. Carlos March Delgado handed the Alba chair to his son Juan March de la Lastra in 2025. Entry is a 1996 Forbes family listing, not an individual.
interesting_fact: In 2025 Carlos March Delgado stepped down as chairman of Corporación Financiera Alba and was replaced by his son Juan March de la Lastra, who already chaired Banca March.
deep_cut_fact: The family's Fundación Juan March runs the Museo de Arte Abstracto Español inside Cuenca's famous Hanging Houses; painter Fernando Zóbel donated its collection to the foundation in 1980.
notes: Family entry, not one person; identity_confirmed set to uncertain because the 1996 Forbes record lists no source or individual. Most relevant living figure: Juan March de la Lastra. Alba holds stakes in industrial/energy-related companies, a possible podcast angle.

name: Stanislaus Turnauer
current_role: Owner and Chairman of the Supervisory Board, Constantia Industries AG (Vienna)
profile: Born 1970, Stanislaus Turnauer is the grandson of Herbert Turnauer, founder of Austria's Constantia group, and head of the discreet Turnauer family. He owns the industrial holding Constantia Industries (approx. 3,400 staff, ~EUR 758m sales) whose companies include Fundermax (wood-based panels) and Isovolta (electrical insulating materials and composites). He moved from the management board to the supervisory board in June 2017.
interesting_fact: Group company Isovolta makes electrical insulating materials, laminates and composites used by around 20 industries, including generator/machinery makers and aviation, from bases in Austria, the US, Mexico, China and India.

public_contacts.value: https://isovolta.com/ (Isovolta contact form, a Constantia Industries company)

notes: Described by trend. as a very discreet family (~EUR 1.25bn). No direct Constantia Industries contact found; CEO is Erlfried Taurer. Avoid political-donation (ILAG/Ibiza) topics. Insulation for generators/electrification is a possible energy hook.

name: Lu Zhongfang
current_role: Major shareholder, Offcn Education Technology (中公教育, SZSE: 002607); no executive role
profile: Lu Zhongfang (鲁忠芳) retired from a pesticides factory in Jilin Province in 1993 and invested in civil-service exam prep firm Offcn in 1999. She is the mother of Offcn chairman Li Yongxin (Forbes spells it Liu) and held about 34% of Offcn in 2022, when she transferred 5.51% to a Hunan fund. Offcn completed a backdoor listing on the Shenzhen exchange in 2019.
interesting_fact: When Offcn raised capital in 2010, Lu subscribed 6 million yuan in cash for a 60% stake, making a retired factory worker the controlling shareholder of what became one of China's largest exam-prep companies.

public_contacts.value: ir@offcn.com (Offcn board secretary / IR, per 2024 annual report summary)

notes: Elderly, entirely private passive shareholder; no public profile or interviews. Any outreach would realistically go to her son Li Yongxin via Offcn IR. Input lists industry as automotive, which is wrong (education). Avoid share-pledge topics.

name: Xi Chao
current_role: Director and co-founder, Neway Valve (Suzhou) Co., Ltd. (纽威股份, SSE: 603699)
profile: Xi Chao (席超) co-founded Suzhou-based Neway Valve in 1997 with Wang Baoqing, Lu Bin and Cheng Zhangwen, and serves as a director. Neway grew into one of China's largest industrial valve makers, supplying upstream, midstream and downstream oil & gas, power, nuclear and new-energy projects, with sales hubs in the Netherlands, Italy, Singapore, the UAE and Nigeria. It listed in Shanghai in 2014.
interesting_fact: Neway has expanded abroad with a valve factory in Vietnam and regional subsidiaries in Europe (2011, Netherlands), Italy (2012, Milan valve cluster), Singapore (2013) and Lagos, Nigeria.
notes: Very low personal profile; little biographical information found. Web-search budget ran out mid-lane, so research here relied on the company site only. Strong energy-industry hook (oil & gas, nuclear, LNG/new-energy valves). Route via company board secretary.

name: Larry Silverstein
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Silverstein Properties (New York)
profile: Brooklyn-born developer (b. 1931) who co-founded Silverstein Properties with his father in 1957 and built a portfolio of office, residential and retail towers. He leased the World Trade Center in July 2001, seven weeks before 9/11, and spent two decades rebuilding 7, 4 and 3 WTC (2 and 5 WTC planned). His firm also owns LA's U.S. Bank Tower and Manhattan's tallest residential tower downtown, 30 Park Place.
interesting_fact: He usually held breakfast meetings at Windows on the World atop the North Tower, but on the morning of 9/11 his wife insisted he keep a medical appointment, which likely saved his life.
deep_cut_fact: Before real estate he was a music kid: he played piano, loved classical music and attended New York's High School of Music and Art; he met his wife Klara while working at a summer camp in college. Brooklyn Law School named him its 2026 Alumnus of the Year.

public_contacts.value: mgrace@Rubenstein.com (Rubenstein, listed as media contact on Silverstein news releases)

notes: Age 95; accessible to press historically (many interviews). Avoid dwelling on 9/11 insurance litigation. Company now run day-to-day by his son and CEO team; press office is responsive route.

name: Betty Ang
current_role: President and co-founder, Monde Nissin Corporation (PSE: MONDE)
profile: Betty T. Ang, an Assumption College business graduate, co-founded Monde Nissin in 1979 with her late father-in-law Hidajat Darmono and built it into the Philippines' leading biscuit and instant-noodle maker (Lucky Me!, SkyFlakes, Fita). Monde Nissin's June 2021 IPO raised 55.9 billion pesos, then the country's largest, and it owns UK meat-alternative brand Quorn.
interesting_fact: Forbes once called her 'one of Asia's most mysterious tycoons'; she rarely gives interviews despite running one of the Philippines' biggest food companies.
deep_cut_fact: Monde Nissin's 1991 launch of Lucky Me! Pancit Canton was the first dry stir-fry pouched noodle in the Philippine market and created a category worth over 10 billion pesos by 2020; the company's very first products in 1979 were Nissin Butter Coconut biscuits and Nissin Wafer.
notes: Extremely private; husband Hoediono Kweefanus is vice-chairman. Avoid Quorn impairment/losses topics. Route via Monde Nissin corporate communications.
